items.title: Haywood Hillyer Interview, 1958-05-04
items.q: I know one man here, past Chris Jan, I can't remember his name, but, uh, he got some of his old cronies, to come over from New Orleans

ctx.x: Oh, Wild Bill, yeah. But, I don't know, Celestan, of course, is dead, but his band is still carrying on, and it's doing pretty well. It's still playing for parties, and they have, I don't know, all the teenage dancers now, they don't have Celestan. I don't know, he plays, I think he plays at some debutante parties now, too, doesn't he? I've heard of him. Oh, in Celestan's time? Yeah. Yeah. I've heard of him, you know, playing at several debutante parties. And, I don't know, still spell out. Okay. I'm sorry. I do.…

Testing, one, two, three. Do you want to say, just say a word first, just see how you pick up? Testing, one, two, three. Just say something in the normal tone of voice you're going to talk in. I have been requested by Haywood Hilliard to give you some history on the New Orleans Jazz of the city of New Orleans. This is Jack Kerrigan speaking. In 1915, I was born March of the 18th, 1900. And, my first contact with jazz was when I lived in Hammond around 1917 at the old Oaks Hotel. Saturday night dances used to be…
